title.name: Stone by Stone
title.subtitle: The town and palace of Olite
menu.easy.note: More cards, more plays, no season limit and only good news.
menu.normal.note: Finish the town before three years are up.
intro.1: Navarre, about 650 years ago. Olite is a small town among wheatfields and vineyards.
intro.2: King Charles III, known as the Noble, likes Olite so much that he wants to live there.
intro.3: But a palace needs a strong town behind it. Start with the houses, the bread, the wine and the walls!
outro.1: Over the years, Olite gained one of the richest palaces of its time in Europe: towers, hanging gardens and even lions.
outro.2: The Royal Palace of Olite still stands. You can visit it and climb its towers!

card.house.name: House
card.house.text: +2 people. They pay 1 coin in autumn.
card.house.history: The town's houses were built of stone, brick and timber.
card.field.name: Wheatfield
card.field.text: +3 bread in spring, summer and autumn.
card.field.history: Wheat gave the daily bread; almost everyone worked the land.
card.vineyard.name: Vineyard
card.vineyard.history: Olite has been ringed by vineyards for centuries; wine was one of its riches.
card.market.name: Market
card.market.history: The market sold wine, grain, cloth and tools.
card.quarry.name: Quarry
card.quarry.history: Stone for the buildings came from nearby quarries.
card.mill.name: Mill
card.mill.history: Mills used the power of water to grind the grain.
card.press.name: Wine press
card.press.history: In the press, grapes were trodden for the juice that became wine.
card.wall.name: Town walls
card.wall.text: They protect the town. Part of the goal!
card.wall.history: Olite was ringed by walls; parts of them can still be seen.
card.marketday.name: Market day
card.marketday.text: +1 coin, and you sell all your wine at 2 each.
card.marketday.history: On fair days people came from all around.
card.harvest.name: Harvest help
card.harvest.history: At harvest the whole family worked, children too.
card.vereda.name: Vereda (auzolan)
card.vereda.history: In Navarre neighbours worked together on shared jobs: the vereda, or auzolan.
card.merchant.name: Merchant
card.merchant.text: Each season sells up to 2 wine at 2 each.
card.merchant.history: Merchants carried Olite's wine to other towns and kingdoms.
card.mason.name: Stonemason
card.mason.text: +1 stone every season. No walls without one.
card.mason.history: Masons cut the stone; some carved their mark on the blocks.
card.carpenter.name: Carpenter
card.carpenter.text: Everything you build costs 1 less timber.
card.carpenter.history: Carpenters made beams, roofs, scaffolds and carts.
card.stonecart.name: Stone cart
card.stonecart.history: Ox carts brought the stone from the quarry.
card.timberraft.name: Pyrenean timber
card.timberraft.history: Some timber came down from the Pyrenees on log rafts, by river.

fact.charles: Charles III the Noble ruled Navarre from 1387 to 1425 and made Olite one of his favourite homes.
fact.leonor: Queen Leonor of Trastámara, Charles III's wife, also lived in the palace at Olite.
fact.gardens: The palace is said to have had hanging gardens, with trees planted high on its walls.
fact.lions: The king kept exotic animals at Olite: lions, camels and faraway birds are mentioned.
fact.wine: Olite's wine was so prized that it was served at court and sold far away.
fact.craftspeople: Christian, Jewish and Mudéjar craftspeople from Navarre and other kingdoms worked on the palace.
fact.fire: In 1813, in the war against Napoleon, the palace was burned so the French could not use it.
fact.restoration: The palace was restored in the 20th century; today you can visit and climb its towers.
